title: Self-Avoiding Garden Walks
description:
## Task

A garden is a grid of open tiles (`.`) and hedges (`#`). A walker starts on the top-left tile and wants to reach the bottom-right tile, stepping one tile up, down, left or right at a time onto open tiles. She never steps on the same tile twice. Count the different walks (distinct sequences of tiles) from start to finish.

## Input

- `grid` — a list of equal-length strings made of `.` and `#`.

## Output

The number of distinct walks. It is 0 if the start or the finish is a hedge. When the grid is a single open tile, the empty walk counts, so the answer is 1.

## Example

```python
self_avoiding_garden_walks(['..', '..'])  # returns 2
self_avoiding_garden_walks(['...', '...', '...'])  # returns 12
self_avoiding_garden_walks(['.#', '#.'])  # returns 0
```

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ rows, columns ≤ 6 and rows * columns ≤ 30
- The answer fits in a normal 64-bit integer.
